scopeNotes: docs/figma/FIGMA_WORKFLOW.md's screen list only names 'Admin / Review Queue / Default' explicitly; this task's explicit instruction (source-of-truth priority 1) required designing all meaningful states, so Loading/Empty/Error/Confirm Approve/Mobile were added beyond that one-line baseline, following the same state-expansion precedent M04 and M05 already established for their own screens.

No 'disabled' state was designed as a separate frame: not meaningful for a queue/list view on its own (the closest disabled-adjacent moment — buttons mid-action, e.g. 'Approving...'/'Ignoring...' — is a frontend in-flight concern per DESIGN.md 12.4/25 'Loading state must preserve button dimensions', not a distinct Figma state), consistent with M05's same reasoning for its own module.

'Failed' finding status was NOT modeled as a distinct badge/card variant in this module: a review queue by definition only surfaces PENDING findings awaiting a human decision (per ARCHITECTURE.md's admin review gate design and DESIGN.md section 19's example, which only shows Pending items). Findings with status=FAILED are out of scope for a review queue and remain a Findings-list/Finding-detail concern (M04/M05).

implementation.backendNotes: No new backend code was required. GET /api/findings (M04's listFindings, status=PENDING) supplies the queue's data; POST /api/findings/:id/approve and /:id/ignore (built by M05, already ADMIN-gated via requireAdmin(), already audit-logged via recordAudit(), already concurrency-safe via conditional updateMany) are called as-is. This satisfies ARCHITECTURE.md/DESIGN.md/docs/MODULES.md's Review Queue scope (pending list, approve, ignore, admin gate, audit trail) without duplicating any business logic.
implementation.frontendNotes: New route apps/web/app/(protected)/admin/review-queue/{page.tsx,loading.tsx} + apps/web/components/admin/review-queue-client.tsx. Reuses existing components as-is: Button, FindingStatusBadge, ErrorState, EmptyState, Pagination, Skeleton, ConfirmApproveDialog (same dialog M05's Finding Detail already uses). Sidebar's 'Review Queue' nav entry (added during the Figma pass) already linked to /admin/review-queue and required no change. States implemented: default (list + counts), loading (route-level Suspense skeleton), empty ('Nothing to review'), error (retry), confirm-approve (modal), mobile (responsive stacked cards + full-width buttons via Tailwind breakpoints on the same route, matching the M04/M05 convention already established instead of a separate mobile page).
implementation.figmaDeviation: The Figma Default/Mobile frames (42:844/42:849) include a severity filter tab row (All/Critical/High/Medium/Low). This was intentionally NOT implemented: the Finding data model (ARCHITECTURE.md, prisma/schema.prisma) has no severity column, and no severity concept exists anywhere else in the codebase (verified via repo-wide search). Building a severity filter over a field that does not exist would fabricate a non-functional control and violate docs/figma/FIGMA_WORKFLOW.md's 'do not create fake states not supported by the product' rule and CLAUDE.md's 'never silently invent a product requirement.' This is a genuine Figma/data-model gap, not an implementation shortcut — flagged below under knownIssues for a future product decision (add a severity field to Finding, or remove the tabs from Figma).
implementation.integrationNotes: Approve/Ignore actions call the real, already-tested M05 endpoints; a successful action removes the row client-side (it is no longer PENDING) rather than faking local state divorced from the server. Middleware (middleware.ts) already gates /admin/:path* to ADMIN role server-side; the client-only isAdmin check is a UX courtesy on top of that, identical to the pattern FindingDetailClient (M05) already uses.
implementation.testNotes: typecheck (tsc --noEmit): clean. eslint on new files: clean. vitest: all 9 existing test files / 64 tests pass unchanged (approve/ignore routes already have 9+9 tests each from M05, exercised as-is, not modified). next build: succeeds, /admin/review-queue registers as a dynamic route. No live Postgres was available in this environment to smoke-test end-to-end against real data (DATABASE_URL in .env.local is a placeholder, not a real connection string) — verification relied on the existing automated test suite plus static Figma-vs-implementation screenshot comparison, the same constraint implicitly faced by prior modules in this environment.
implementation.securityNotes: No raw secret ever enters this module's code path: FindingSummary (used here) has no snippet/secret field at all (only FindingDetail, used by M05, carries the already-redacted snippet). Authorization enforced server-side twice: middleware.ts redirects non-ADMIN sessions away from /admin/*, and the approve/ignore route handlers independently call requireAdmin() (defense-in-depth, not client-trust). Every approve/ignore action is audit-logged via the existing recordAudit() call inside those routes (unchanged). No token, credential, or raw finding value is logged to console anywhere in the new code.

notes: Design-only pass for M06 (Admin Review Queue) per figma-design-module skill boundary and CLAUDE.md section 3 (one-module rule). Backend review-queue API, server-side state-transition validation, audit logging, admin-role authorization enforcement, and frontend implementation are NOT part of this pass and remain required before M06 can be marked DONE.

Screen set: Default, Loading, Empty, Error, Confirm Approve (modal), Mobile — 6 states total, following DESIGN.md section 19's Review Queue layout and section 26's exact confirmation-dialog copy, extended with Loading/Empty/Error/Mobile per this task's explicit 'include all meaningful states' instruction.

A figma-auditor subagent was launched after the initial design pass for independent read-only verification. It correctly identified a real BLOCKING defect: the Sidebar was not reused as a live component instance (an earlier detachInstance()-based approach to add a 'Review Queue' nav item had broken the live component link across 5 frames). Rather than accept the auditor's finding on faith, it was independently re-verified live against the file first (confirmed: all 5 sidebar nodes were type=FRAME, not INSTANCE) — consistent with the established M04/M05 reconcile-before-trusting practice.

Fixing the blocking issue required a genuine product decision: the Sidebar component's shipped 8-item nav set has no 'Review Queue' slot, and two workaround approaches (repurposing an existing item's label, or overlaying a duplicate on top of one) were tried and both rejected as dishonest/lossy — one silently dropped 'Scan Rules' from the visible nav, the other visually hid it behind an opaque duplicate while leaving it structurally present underneath. The user was asked directly and chose to extend the shared Sidebar component itself (recommended option) over the other two choices offered. The master Sidebar component (7:15, owned by M00 on page '02 — Components') was extended with a real, permanent 9th Nav Item — additive and backward compatible, all 8 original items preserved unchanged.

The auditor's two non-blocking notes were also addressed: mobile action buttons resized from 36px to 44px height to satisfy DESIGN.md section 30's minimum tap-target rule (pagination repositioned and frame resized accordingly, 676px -> 708px); the scrim cosmetic note did not reproduce on direct inspection and required no change.

Did not touch any M01, M02, M03, M04, or M05 existing frame content — only the master Sidebar component on the shared '02 — Components' page was modified (additively), per explicit user authorization, plus new content added to the previously-empty '05 — Admin' page for this module's own 6 frames.
Did not design Rules, Templates, Workers, Users, Marketing, Auth, Tokens, Scan Rules, Overview, Findings-list, or Finding-detail screens — all out of scope for M06.

Module remains CLAIMED, not DONE — this pass intentionally stops at Figma design completion per the one-module rule (CLAUDE.md section 3) and the task's explicit scope boundary (design-only; no frontend/backend code written). Do not automatically start M07 or any other module.
